tagline: Leading energy delivery and generation company serving customers across the Midwest
hero_kpi_rationale: Regulatory Assets are central to WEC's financial model, reflecting the company's ability to recover prudently incurred operating costs and earn an authorized return from regulators. This KPI is essential for assessing the long-term financial viability of a regulated utility business.

kpis.name: Regulatory Assets
kpis.explanation: Assets held pursuant to regulatory accounting guidelines, representing deferred costs recoverable from customers through future rates
kpis.description: Regulatory assets represent deferred costs that management believes are probable of recovery from customers through future rates, in accordance with regulatory orders.
kpis.signal: Key indicator of financial health and cost recoverability for a regulated utility

kpis.name: Interest Rate Risk Exposure
kpis.explanation: Risk exposure from short-term and long-term borrowings and debt financing needs, managed through fixed-rate debt and derivative instruments
kpis.description: WEC manages its interest rate risk exposure by limiting the amount of variable-rate debt and using hedging instruments such as interest rate swaps to mitigate the effects of market fluctuations.
kpis.signal: Significant exposure to interest rate changes impacting future borrowing costs

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Consolidated annual revenue, value extracted from yfinance.income_stmt over the last four reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Revenue of 9.8 Bn € in the latest year

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.description: Net income extracted from yfinance.income_stmt over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Net income of 1.56 Bn € in the latest year

kpis.name: Operating Income
kpis.description: Operating income extracted from yfinance.income_stmt over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Operating income of 2.37 Bn € in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of 51.52 Bn € in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of 22.31 Bn € in the latest year

kpis.name: Cash & Equivalents
kpis.description: Cash & equivalents extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Cash & equivalents of 0.03 Bn € in the latest year

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last seven fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of 0.953 $ in the latest year

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last four reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of 1.148 Bn $ in the latest year

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last four fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Proportion of net income distributed as dividends: 73.6% in the latest year

kpis.name: Ongoing Regulatory Proceedings
kpis.explanation: Ongoing regulatory rate cases and proceedings that determine cost recovery and authorized returns
kpis.description: Ongoing regulatory proceedings in jurisdictions where WEC's utilities operate determine the approval of cost recovery, authorized rate of return, and recovery timing.
kpis.signal: Material impact on future rates, authorized return levels, and cost recoverability

risks.title: Risks related to regulatory assets and tariff-based cost recovery
risks.score_rationale: This risk is explicitly identified as a Critical Audit Matter in the auditor's report. The text emphasizes that future recovery of regulatory assets is not guaranteed and depends entirely on discretionary decisions by regulatory authorities regarding prudence, reasonableness, and recovery timing. This risk is fundamental to WEC's regulated business model.

risks.title: Risk related to accounting estimates for assets and liabilities
risks.score_rationale: Documented in the Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates section of the report. The text highlights that preparing financial statements in accordance with GAAP requires the use of estimates, assumptions, and judgments that could have a material impact. Judgments about future events include the likelihood of project success, legal and regulatory challenges, and expected cost recovery.

risks.title: Risk related to goodwill valuations and impairment tests
risks.score_rationale: Goodwill is sensitive to forecast assumptions and market conditions. Although current tests have not indicated impairment, uncertainty in future forecasts and the potential impact of interest rate changes and regulatory decisions create a risk of future impairment.

risks.title: Risk related to pension and employee benefit costs
risks.score_rationale: Pension costs depend on numerous complex actuarial assumptions (return rates, mortality rates, discount rates) and are sensitive to financial market performance. Interest rate fluctuations can significantly affect pension obligations.

risks.title: Risk related to weather impacts and natural disasters
risks.score_rationale: Although tariffs include a fixed amount for expected restoration costs, severe storms exceeding these provisions may result in significant unrecovered costs and revenue losses, impacting profitability and authorized returns.

risks.title: Risk related to taxation and tax uncertainties
risks.score_rationale: Determining tax expenses, deferred tax assets and liabilities requires complex judgments. Changes in tax legislation, tax rates, or tax audit outcomes could have a material impact on financial results.

risks.title: Risk related to commodity cost fluctuations
risks.score_rationale: High commodity costs increase working capital needs and customer default risk, although tariff-based cost recovery mechanisms exist. Exposure remains significant during periods of price volatility.
